description: This course covers software architecture design and implementation using industry-standard frameworks such as UML, ArchiMate, and the Open Group Architecture Framework (TOGAF). Topics include modeling techniques for layered architectures, microservices, and event-driven systems; architectural patterns like MVC, layered, and microservices; service-oriented architecture (SOA) and its implementation with RESTful APIs; architectural evaluation methods such as the 4+1 view model and the Architecture Tradeoff Analysis Method (ATAM); and the use of tools like Enterprise Architect and Visual Paradigm for diagramming and documentation. The course also covers the application of architectural styles to real-world problems, including performance, scalability, and security considerations in distributed systems.

clos.text: Define key software architecture concepts, including architectural patterns, styles, and quality attributes such as performance and scalability.
Describe the UML and ArchiMate modeling notations and their application in representing software architecture diagrams.
Explain the principles of service-oriented architecture (SOA) and how to implement RESTful APIs using frameworks like Spring Boot and Node.js.
Apply architectural evaluation techniques such as ATAM to analyze tradeoffs between system qualities like security and maintainability.
Implement a software architecture for a distributed system using microservices patterns and cloud-native technologies like Docker and Kubernetes.

topics: Quality Attributes and Their Impact on Architecture
